svg.title: Fig. 185 — The septa of the Nautilus are equiangular spirals
svg.desc: Redrawn from Robert C. Yates, A Handbook on Curves and Their Properties (1947), Fig. 185, page 208. Section: spirals.

g.data-text: The pole O of the spiral. A whorl of the shell is the same shape as the whorl inside it, only larger: every turn multiplies the radius by the same factor (here 3).

Draw the radii at equal angles of 30° to each other. With the dividers lay off on them the lengths r, qr, q²r, … in geometric progression with q = 3^{1/12}: twelve steps of 30° multiply the radius by 3.
Join the points with a French curve: the wall of the shell, the equiangular spiral r = a·e^{kθ} with k = ln 3 / 2π.

Each septum is an arc of an equiangular spiral about O, steeper than the wall: it runs from a point of the inner whorl to the point of the outer whorl that lies 100° further round. Draw one every 30°.
